# Reading the wind

Sailors read the wind from dark patches of ripples on the water, which mark gusts arriving, and from the telltales and the burgee at the masthead. Use it to choose your [[Points of sail]] and when [[Reefing the mainsail]].

## Gusts and lulls

A gust shows as a dark, ruffled patch moving toward the boat. Ease the mainsheet as it hits to keep the boat flat, then trim back in as it passes.

## Wind shifts

A lift lets the boat point higher toward the wind; a header forces it to bear away. Tack on headers to sail the shorter way upwind.
